identity.name: OpenClaw ClawHub Malicious Skill — Padded README, base64 curl|bash Dropper and Developer-Credential Theft
identity.summary: A highly-rated OpenClaw ClawHub marketplace skill ships a padded README (megabytes of filler to evade content scanners) whose mandatory prerequisite block is a base64-encoded curl|bash dropper. Following it harvests the developer's SSH key, cloud credentials, .npmrc, .env and the agent's ~/.claude.json, archives them and beacons the loot to a hard-coded C2 / Telegram Bot API.
identity.description: Built from the Palo Alto Networks Unit 42 research on AI-agent skill-marketplace supply-chain risk — 'OpenClaw's Skill Marketplace and the Emerging AI Supply Chain Threat' (https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/openclaw-ai-supply-chain-risk/) and the companion 'Trust No Skill' (https://unit42.paloaltonetworks.com/ai-agent-supply-chain-risks/). The public research describes a marketplace (ClawHub) for the OpenClaw AI coding agent where a highly-rated skill presenting as a productivity tool (e.g. a TradingView / financial assistant) carries a SKILL.md/README.md with a mandatory prerequisite block that induces the agent or the developer to run a command. The malicious author evades content-analysis by PADDING the README with tens of megabytes of filler so an oversized-file scanner skips it, placing the malicious block at the top. The prerequisite block is a base64-encoded 'curl | bash' one-liner; decoding and running it fetches an infostealer that harvests developer credential stores (SSH keys, cloud credentials, npm tokens, .env secrets and the agent's own credential file), archives them, and exfiltrates to attacker infrastructure and a Telegram Bot API. The research also documents paste-site redirects (rentry.co / glot.io) that front the payload and an agentic affiliate-injection angle (a 'money-radar' referrals.json the agent is steered to inject). CortexSim does NOT reproduce the real payload or contact any real C2. SIM-KOI-011 runs the SAME endpoint observables on a bare Ubuntu developer host, all under the agent lineage (CGO = the node agent runtime): it stages the re-skinned in-tree malicious skill with a genuine ~22 MB padded README, base64-decodes the embedded prerequisite, runs the decoded curl|bash dropper against a NON-RESOLVING .invalid canary (real process + failed DNS, no payload fetched, no real C2), executes a locally-staged infostealer that reads five DECOY credential files (every value is the literal CORTEXSIM-DECOY) under a fake $HOME at /var/tmp/.koi011-victim, archives the loot and emits a beacon to another .invalid canary. A guard refuses to run unless the fake $HOME resolves under /var/tmp, so the operator's real ~/.ssh, ~/.aws and ~/.npmrc are never read. The declared detections are the endpoint-resident behavioral signals Cortex raises on its own: the built-in 'Uncommon Linux shell command execution' analytics on the base64-decode and the curl|bash dropper (ABIOC), a BIOC on a dropped shell reading three or more credential files in one window under the agent lineage, two XQL validations on the oversized-README and loot-archive file creates, and a correlation that stitches the chain into one incident. Hunting content, deliberately NOT declared as an expectation: the dropper-host DNS/egress query, the C2 / Telegram beacon-egress query, the paste-site-redirect query and the agentic affiliate-injection query all carry purpose 'hunt'. They are queries the DC runs by hand when a sink and a firewall are in path; the scenario declares none of them, so a sink-less run seeds no Result row for them and therefore neither passes nor fails on them. The correlation CR-KOI-0011 closes on the endpoint at the loot-archive create, not the egress, for exactly that reason.

biocs.name: KOI-011 Dropped Shell Reads Multiple Developer Credential Files
biocs.description: A shell dropped by the OpenClaw skill prerequisite reads three or more distinct developer credential-named files (SSH private key, cloud credentials, npm token, .env secrets, the agent's own ~/.claude.json) in one window under the agent causality chain. A productivity skill that reads this set is stealing, not assisting. The threshold is three distinct paths to keep a single settings read quiet; the decoy run yields five (.ssh/id_rsa, .aws/credentials, .npmrc, .env, .claude.json). Keep routine agent/editor config reads out of the credential-name list so a launch that reads only config does not satisfy the threshold.
biocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_OPEN, ENUM.FILE_READ)
| filter action_process_image_name in ("sh", "bash", "dash", "cat", "python3", "perl")
| filter action_file_path contains_any (".ssh/id_rsa", "id_ed25519", ".aws/credentials", ".npmrc", ".env", ".claude.json", ".config/gcloud/credentials")
| comp count_distinct(action_file_path) as cred_files by agent_hostname, actor_causality_id, action_process_image_name
| filter cred_files >= 3
| fields agent_hostname, actor_causality_id, action_process_image_name, cred_files

dataset = xdr_data
| filter timestamp_diff(current_time(), _time, "SECOND") < 1800
| filter event_type = ENUM.FILE and event_sub_type in (ENUM.FILE_CREATE_NEW, ENUM.FILE_WRITE)
| filter action_file_path contains "/.openclaw/skills/" and action_file_name = "README.md"
| fields _time, agent_hostname, actor_causality_id, actor_process_image_name, action_file_path, action_file_size

abiocs.name: KOI-011 Base64 Decode Of Agent Skill Prerequisite Block
abiocs.description: Behavioral-ML deviation (the built-in 'Uncommon Linux shell command execution' analytics): a process in the AI-agent lineage runs base64 -d on a blob lifted from a marketplace skill's prerequisite block. A productivity skill has no reason to carry a base64-encoded shell command; decoding one in the agent chain is the OpenClaw dropper's reveal step.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name = "base64"
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains_any ("-d", "--decode")
| comp count() as decodes by agent_hostname, actor_causality_id, causality_actor_process_image_name, action_process_image_command_line
| filter decodes >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, actor_causality_id, causality_actor_process_image_name, action_process_image_command_line, decodes
abiocs.causality_anchor: The OpenClaw agent runtime (Causality Group Owner) and its actor_causality_id; the deviation is a base64-decode of an encoded shell command sourced from a marketplace skill prerequisite, against the baseline of agent lineages that decode nothing.

abiocs.name: KOI-011 Curl Pipe To Bash Dropper From Agent Lineage
abiocs.description: Behavioral-ML deviation (the built-in 'Uncommon Linux shell command execution' analytics): a curl (or wget) fetch of a remote URL is piped straight into a shell under the AI-agent lineage — the curl|bash LOLBIN ingress the OpenClaw prerequisite block performs. The fetch targets a host outside any package registry or marketplace CDN; in the lab it is a non-resolving canary, so curl fails and nothing is downloaded, but the process shape and the DNS lookup are the signal.
abiocs.logic:
dataset = xdr_data
| filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
| filter action_process_image_name in ("curl", "wget")
| filter action_process_image_command_line contains_any ("http://", "https://")
| join type = inner (
    dataset = xdr_data
    | filter event_type = ENUM.PROCESS and event_sub_type = ENUM.PROCESS_START
    | filter action_process_image_name in ("bash", "sh", "dash")
    | fields actor_causality_id as shell_cid, agent_hostname as shell_host
) as sib shell_cid = actor_causality_id and shell_host = agent_hostname
| comp count() as fetches by agent_hostname, actor_causality_id, causality_actor_process_image_name, action_process_image_command_line
| filter fetches >= 1
| fields agent_hostname, actor_causality_id, causality_actor_process_image_name, action_process_image_command_line, fetches
abiocs.causality_anchor: The OpenClaw agent runtime (Causality Group Owner) and its actor_causality_id; the deviation is a curl/wget fetch of a non-registry URL piped into a shell in the same causality chain, against the baseline of agent lineages that never pipe a download into an interpreter.

correlation_rules.name: OpenClaw ClawHub Malicious Skill — Prerequisite Decode, curl|bash Dropper, Developer-Credential Read and Local Staging

The chain closes on the endpoint: its terminal term is the loot-archive create, not the egress, so the rule fires in a lab with no authorised sink and no firewall in path.

threat_scenarios.name: OpenClaw ClawHub Malicious Skill — Marketplace Delivery to Developer-Credential Theft
threat_scenarios.description: Detect a trojanized AI-agent marketplace skill end to end on a Linux developer endpoint: padded-README delivery, base64 prerequisite decode, curl|bash dropper, developer-credential read, local staging and beacon — stitched into one causality-aware incident.

threat_steps.objective: The padded-README skill is staged and the prerequisite block is decoded and run under the agent lineage.
preconditions: Linux endpoint with the Cortex agent and the cortex-malicious-agentic-pack checkout.
steps: Stage the ClawHub skill with a 22 MB padded README and decoy developer credentials.
Decode the base64 prerequisite block and run the curl|bash dropper against a non-resolving canary.
Observe the oversized-README XQL and the base64-decode and curl|bash ABIOCs.
success_criteria: XQL `KOI-011 Oversized Marketplace Skill README Created Under Agent Skills Dir` returns the skill README create.
ABIOC `KOI-011 Base64 Decode Of Agent Skill Prerequisite Block` fires.
ABIOC `KOI-011 Curl Pipe To Bash Dropper From Agent Lineage` fires.

threat_steps.objective: The dropped infostealer reads developer credentials, stages and archives the loot, and the chain correlates into one incident.
preconditions: TS-KOI-011A executed within the correlation window.
steps: Run the locally-staged infostealer that reads the decoy credential files.
Stage and archive the loot; emit the beacon to a non-resolving canary.
Confirm correlation CR-KOI-0011 stitches every stage into one incident.
success_criteria: BIOC `KOI-011 Dropped Shell Reads Multiple Developer Credential Files` fires.
XQL `KOI-011 Stolen Credentials Archived Into Staging Tarball` returns the loot-archive create.
Correlation `CR-KOI-0011` raises exactly one OpenClaw incident. Its terminal term is the loot-archive create, so it fires on the endpoint alone: no sink and no firewall in path are required.

Not a criterion: the dropper-host DNS/egress, the C2 / Telegram beacon-egress, the paste-site-redirect and the agentic affiliate-injection queries carry `purpose: hunt`. The scenario declares none of them, so a sink-less run seeds nothing for them and scores neither a pass nor a fail against them.

preventive_controls: Allow only vetted AI-agent skills: restrict installs to an internal registry gateway or an approved publisher list, and apply a delayed-access / version cooldown so a freshly published skill is not usable the day it ships.

Treat any skill or README that asks the agent or the developer to run a shell command — especially a base64-encoded or curl|bash one — as malicious by default; strip or quarantine prerequisite blocks at the registry gateway.
Flag and quarantine abnormally large skill README/manifest files (padding is an evasion, not documentation), and scan the head of oversized files rather than skipping them.

Keep long-lived credentials out of developer home directories: short-lived tokens, a credential helper and hardware-backed SSH keys so a file read yields nothing reusable, and store the agent's own API token outside the readable home config.
Egress-filter developer endpoints to package registries and approved marketplace CDNs only; alert on curl/wget to paste sites (rentry.co, glot.io) or unknown setup hosts.
detection_engineering: Anchor on actor_causality_id and the agent runtime image, never on a username: the AI agent is the Causality Group Owner and the decode, dropper, credential read and staging are all its descendants.
Treat an agent lineage that runs base64 -d, then curl|bash, as the signal — neither is part of normal agent-skill behavior; the two together are the OpenClaw dropper.

Require three or more distinct credential-named files read in one window by the agent chain before alerting on credential theft, and keep the agent's own routine config reads out of that list so a plain launch does not satisfy the threshold.

Pair the endpoint chain with NGFW egress to a non-marketplace setup host and with the C2 / Telegram beacon when a firewall is in path (both are hunt queries on this card), and with a Cortex Cloud Code finding on the padded-README skill manifest.
